body:
There's already no confusion on whether array elements are sorted (arrays are **not** dictionaries), nor on whether nested dictionaries are affected ("**any** [Dictionary]s"). It's such an odd overcorrection.

Also, why are these here notes in the first place? Not just the one added in this PR. Notes are for tangential information. What the parameters _even do_ is not "tangential".

```suggestion
				If [param sort_keys] is [code]true[/code], the keys of any [Dictionary]s are sorted alphabetically when converting to JSON. If [param sort_keys] is [code]false[/code], the order of the keys is preserved.
```

I believe (but I may be very wrong here even as I checked) that this method goes through a process similar to `Dictionary.sort()`, so perhaps it's worth mentioning. Neither methods are truly "alphabetical", but I'm not sure describing Unicode code points would be beneficial here.
And finally, to be ridiculously pedantic, what `sort_keys` does when it's `false` can be inferred by the whole explanation.

```suggestion
				If [param sort_keys] is [code]true[/code], the keys of any converted dictionary are sorted alphabetically (see also [method Dictionary.sort]).
```

body:
I'm not sure why this section needed changing, since the original issue is not about this, but I find this change to be **way** too verbose without solving the awkward wording of the original. The only good thing to come out of it is describing what happens with an "empty string".

I would suggest keeping this out of the PR, but maybe I can come up with a proper replacement at a later time.
